name: Mean cell haemoglobin concentration
summary: MCHC is how concentrated the haemoglobin is inside red blood cells. It varies little in healthy people.

high.meaning: A high MCHC is uncommon. It can be a measurement artefact or point to an inherited red cell shape condition.
commonCauses: Sample problems (e.g. clumping or high blood fats)

low.meaning: A low MCHC means red cells are paler than usual, most often from iron deficiency.
